site.title: Bayview Books for Kids · Oakland
site.description: An Oakland-based non-profit putting books into the hands of kids in Title-I schools across Alameda County. Since 2019 we've distributed 12,400 books to 47 schools.
site.author: Constance Olivera
site.tagline: A book in the hand of every Title-I third grader in Alameda County.

props.text: 12,400 books delivered to 47 Title-I schools in Alameda County since September 2019.

Forty-three percent of the third graders we served last fall did not have a single age-appropriate book at home. Not a low number. Not a high number. The number. We exist to change that one classroom at a time, with one program, in partnership with the schools who already know what their students need.

props.text: Why this work, why now, why this way.

In 2018 the Oakland Unified School District closed five elementary school libraries inside a single budget cycle. The closures hit Title-I schools first. The district's own data showed third-grade reading-level gaps grew six percentage points in two years across the affected schools. We started Bayview Books for Kids in the fall of 2019 to address one specific piece of that picture: kids could no longer take books home.

We do not run reading programs. We do not duplicate work. We partner with teachers and librarians who already know which kids need what — they tell us what to bring, we bring it. Our partner schools include Acorn Woodland, Bridges Academy, EnCompass, Esperanza, Fred T. Korematsu Discovery, Greenleaf, Manzanita Community, Markham, and Sankofa Academy. Every book is age-appropriate. Every book is theirs to keep.

The single most common question we get from new donors is whether digital readers would be cheaper. We have run that math three times. They are not, once you account for charging, theft, and the fact that 67 percent of our families said in a 2023 survey that they want their child to own a physical book. We are not anti-tech. We are pro-the-thing-the-families-asked-for.

props.quote: I have been a third-grade teacher at Acorn Woodland for fourteen years. Bayview Books has been the most reliable partner I have ever worked with. They show up the week they say. Every box is curated. My students recognize their names on the shelf.
props.author: Jacqueline Mendez-Cole
props.role: 3rd Grade Teacher · Acorn Woodland Elementary · Oakland

props.quote: I have volunteered with Bayview every Saturday morning since November 2022. We sort, we label, we pack. It is the calmest two hours of my week. I am 71 and I have learned the names of 140 fourth graders by way of their reading lists.
props.author: Hank Bremerton

props.quote: We met with Constance and her board in December 2023 to talk about a $40,000 grant. She walked into the meeting with a 14-page spending plan and a printout of every book delivery for the prior school year. That is what changed my mind, not the pitch.
props.author: Renata Olivierre
props.role: Program Officer · East Bay Community Foundation

props.quote: My daughter Adriana brought home Brown Girl Dreaming in February. She finished it in a week and asked for the next Jacqueline Woodson book. We did not have library cards. Now we do. I do not know who you are exactly but thank you.
props.author: Yesenia Torres
props.role: Parent · Sankofa Academy family · East Oakland
